The loss function 1 for $\mathbf { M u C A L }$ training incorporatesatemperatureparameter $\tau$ ,which modulates the sharpness of the similarity distribution within a batch. Lower values of $\tau$ lead to sharper distributions that focus more on the most similar instances, while higher values result in smoother, more uniform distributions.

Notably, for memory-intensive training setups such as cross-encoder architectures,a smaller $\tau$ is particularly beneficial when using lower-precision computations (e.g., bfloat16),as it helps maintain numerical stability and mitigates precision-related artefacts. In our experiments, we set $\tau = 0 . 2$
